solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Get names wrong, having mixed briefly with everyone

parts.note: MISC is the short form of miscellaneous, meaning mixed
everyone means all

explanation.surface: Someone at a gathering mingles with everyone for a while but keeps getting names wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To miscall is to call someone or something by the incorrect name.

clue.text: False claim about a lot of states, such as Oklahoma!

indicators.note: the shuffled letters of claim go round, about, the abbreviation for the states
a false version of the word claim is a counterfeit arrangement of its letters

parts.note: the US, a federation of fifty states, is a lot of states

explanation.surface: Someone makes a bogus claim concerning a large number of American states, such as Oklahoma.
explanation.walkthrough: Oklahoma! with its exclamation mark is the Rodgers and Hammerstein show, not the state the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma! is a famous stage show with songs, an example of the genre.

clue.text: Behind and extremely lazy, admonished thus?

parts.note: the stern is the back or behind of a ship

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, the first and last, of lazy

parts.note: outer letters L and Y

explanation.surface: Someone lagging behind and very idle gets told off in this manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe telling-off is delivered in a harsh, strict manner, as the question mark hints.

clue.text: Contribution to total amount for ill-fated mission

indicators.note: Contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A donation towards the full sum raised for a doomed expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: The Alamo was the Texas mission besieged in 1836, where all the defenders died.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo was a Spanish mission building whose defenders were all killed in the siege of 1836.

clue.text: Spring in a small resort? Quite a big one, actually

definitions.note: the 'one' stands for a resort, the surface sense of the previous word

indicators.note: the spring goes inside the re-sorted letters
read as re-sort, the letters of a small are sorted again into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: A spring at a little holiday town, which turns out to be no little place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort?' does double duty: re-sort signals the anagram, and the resort is what 'one' in the definition refers to. The city is on Gran Canaria in the Canary Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canary Islands capital is a large tourist destination, so a sizable holiday resort.

clue.text: One way to make the most of gold accumulation

parts.note: back is one way or direction to go

indicators.note: to make the next letters go that way, back, so they are written in the opposite order
the most of a word is all but its last letter

explanation.surface: Advice on how best to exploit a hoard of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: BACK does two jobs: it is 'one way', and 'to make' the trimmed gold, GOL, go that way reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlog is a pile of work or orders built up and waiting to be dealt with.

clue.text: Encouragement good person got, following negative response

indicators.note: the saint comes after, following, the jeer

parts.note: a boo is a jeer, a negative response from a crowd
ST, short for saint, a crossword good person

explanation.surface: A worthy person receives a pep talk after being turned down.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost is a lift in morale or support, something that heartens someone.

clue.text: You reportedly train specially, entering contest and beginning to play

indicators.note: the sound and the reworked letters go inside the contest word

parts.note: a cup is a contest, as in a football cup competition

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is heard spoken, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: the word you is said aloud as the letter U

indicators.note: specially suggests the letters of train are arranged in a particular new way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to train in a particular way for a competition and the start of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' suggests a game, but it is a theatre show; a cup is a sporting competition, and 'reportedly' gives the letter that sounds like you.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtain-up is the moment a theatre performance starts, when the stage curtain rises.

clue.text: Greek character holding a lively dance

indicators.note: holding means the Greek letter contains the A

parts.note: lambda is the eleventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek person clutching something while doing a spirited dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person from Greece, but it is a letter of the Greek alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The lambada is a fast, sensual Brazilian partner dance popular in the late 1980s.

clue.text: Conspirator concealing bungled plan for use of weapons

indicators.note: the conspirator's name hides the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: Guy Fawkes, the Gunpowder Plot conspirator

indicators.note: bungled means messed up, so the letters of plan are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A plotter hides a failed scheme involving firearms.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy Fawkes tried to blow up Parliament in 1605; Britain marks it on Bonfire Night.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunplay is the shooting or brandishing of guns, the handling of firearms.

clue.text: Regard tools as things children can have fun with

definitions.text: things children can have fun with

parts.note: to regard is to see or look at
saws are cutting tools

explanation.surface: Treat workshop tools as playthings for children.
explanation.definitionFit: Seesaws are playground planks pivoted in the middle that children ride up and down.

clue.text: Mistreated as Roman galley slave, for example

indicators.note: mistreated suggests the words as Roman are handled badly, rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Roman galley slave is abused.
explanation.definitionFit: Galley slaves rowed the ship, so each was one who pulls an oar.

clue.text: Both he and she start with one — not I

definitions.text: Both he and she start with one — not I

parts.words: Both he and she start with one — not I
parts.note: the pronouns he and she begin with H and S, letters that are not vowels, whereas the pronoun I begins with a vowel

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is about the spelling of pronouns, not people: H and S are non-vowel letters, while I is a vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: A consonant is any speech letter other than a vowel, such as H or S.

clue.text: Benefit of something that may save face, say

indicators.note: say signals the words are heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a veil covers and protects the face

explanation.surface: The advantage of something that preserves one's dignity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save face' looks like the idiom about dignity, but here a veil literally shields a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail means use or advantage, as in to no avail.

clue.text: Film actor penniless at first

indicators.note: P is the abbreviation for penny, and it is removed from the front

parts.note: a player is an actor

explanation.surface: A movie star who was broke at the start of their career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' wants to be a movie, but it is a thin coating.
explanation.definitionFit: A film is a thin coating or sheet spread over a surface.

clue.text: Not altogether sure, though they had a second opinion

indicators.note: Not altogether says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: People were uncertain, so they consulted someone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To have rethought is to have reconsidered and formed a new view.

clue.text: Queen receiving warning ahead of time, in short

indicators.note: the queen's name takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: Mary, as in Queen Mary

indicators.note: the omen comes before the T

parts.note: an omen is a warning sign

explanation.surface: A monarch gets an early warning, briefly put.
explanation.definitionFit: Something momentary lasts only an instant, so it is brief.

clue.text: Fairest winner of all?

parts.note: echoes Snow White's mirror, 'who is the fairest of them all', describing the victor of a global beauty pageant

explanation.walkthrough: The wording echoes the wicked queen's mirror in Snow White; the winner of an international beauty contest is crowned the fairest.
explanation.definitionFit: The title goes to the winner of an annual international beauty pageant.

clue.text: They help their favourites in top sets, wrongly

indicators.note: wrongly says the letters of in top sets are put in a wrong, new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Teachers who unfairly place pupils they like in the highest ability groups.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepotists favour relatives or friends when handing out jobs or advantages.

clue.text: Like the lion's share? By no means

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the lion's share is the bigger part, so it is literally more than a half
second meaning: British ironic slang, as in '... bad', used to deny half-measures; not to any small degree

explanation.walkthrough: The British phrase means 'very much indeed', the opposite of what it says; read literally, it describes a portion bigger than a half.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is British slang for emphatic agreement, and literally describes a portion larger than a half.

clue.text: Gambler holding spades and joker

indicators.note: the gambler contains the S

parts.note: a punter is a bettor or gambler
S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: A card player keeping a spade and the joker in their hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joker' looks like the playing card, but it is a person who makes jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A punster is someone who makes puns, a wisecracking wordplay humorist.

clue.text: Fare from Italy by air, initially

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by or past

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of air

parts.note: first letter A

explanation.surface: Travel costs from Italy when flying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price; it is food.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare means food, and pasta is the staple Italian dish.

clue.text: Detach a line for divers

parts.note: to sever is to cut off or detach

explanation.surface: Cut free a rope for scuba divers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' looks like underwater swimmers, but it is the old adjective meaning various.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers, stressed on the first syllable, is an archaic adjective for sundry or various, a number of.

clue.text: Dunce making appearance before principal

indicators.note: the appearance comes first, before the principal

parts.note: an air is a manner or appearance
a principal or head of a school

explanation.surface: A dim pupil shows up in front of the headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: An airhead is a slang term for a stupid or empty-headed person.

clue.text: Last piece of concert on radio is dance music

indicators.note: on radio means the letter as radio operators spell it out in the phonetic alphabet

parts.note: the final letter of concert, which radio operators call out by its code word

explanation.surface: The final item at a broadcast concert is a dance tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio operators use the NATO phonetic alphabet, where T is spoken as TANGO.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is an Argentine ballroom dance and the music written for it.

clue.text: Admit into golf club closer to the sea

indicators.note: the admission goes into the club

parts.note: a driver is the club used for long tee shots
to own up is to admit

explanation.surface: Let someone join a golf club near the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf club' reads as a members' club, but it is a stick for hitting the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Downriver means further along the flow of a river, towards its mouth and the sea.

clue.text: Personal records, with assistance, set up on tracks

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first part sits on top of the second
in a down clue, set up means written upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: aid means help or assistance
RY, short for railway, tracks

explanation.surface: Keeping one's own log, with help, while on the railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary is a daily personal journal of events and thoughts.

clue.text: Headless chicken or other bird

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: chicken means cowardly, craven

explanation.surface: A chicken with its head off, or a different bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chicken' looks like a bird, but here it means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black corvid, a bird other than a chicken.

clue.text: From tyrant, I guarded island

indicators.note: from says the answer is taken out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: the answer sits across these words

explanation.surface: Someone protected an island from a despot.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is a Caribbean island, part of the nation Antigua and Barbuda.

clue.text: American hero accepting second defeat? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the hero takes the S inside

parts.note: Paul Revere, rider who warned of the British advance in 1775

explanation.surface: An American hero endures a second loss, or quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' is a further nod to the answer's other sense, the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse is a setback or misfortune, especially a military one.

clue.text: Trees that will decay, finally, before all the others

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of the three following words

parts.note: last letter T
last letter L
last letter Y

explanation.surface: Trees that are going to rot, in the end, ahead of everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Firstly means in the first place, ahead of the rest in a list.

clue.text: Enticingly offered divine fish inside

indicators.note: the fishing goes inside the two Ds

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, a divine or clergyman
to angle is to fish

explanation.surface: A clergyman with a fish within held out something tempting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like an adjective but is a noun for a clergyman, and DD is the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle something is to hold it out as a temptation or bait.
